title: French Onion Burgers with Gruyère
changes_from_base: Thyme-seasoned thick patties are seared then finished in a low oven, and the buns are spread with a slow-cooked balsamic onion jam and grilled under a blanket of Gruyère; frisée replaces lettuce. My own onion jam replaces the referenced one.
summary: Deeply caramelised onions give these beef patties a rich, sweet-savoury depth, crowned with bubbling melted Gruyère and peppery frisée.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Jam
steps.text: Melt 30 g butter in a large frying pan over medium-low, add 2 large thinly sliced onions and ¼ tsp fine salt, cover for 10 min, then uncover and cook 35-40 min, stirring often, until deep golden; stir in 1 tbsp light brown sugar and 1 tbsp balsamic vinegar and cook 2 min until sticky.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Combine 1½ tsp finely chopped fresh thyme, ½ tsp fine salt and ¼ tsp ground black pepper, then loosely shape 800 g beef mince into 4 patties 2 cm thick with a 1 cm dip in the centre of each; season with the thyme mix.

steps.title: Brown
steps.text: Heat 5 ml oil in the pan over high until just smoking, add patties dip side up and cook 2-4 min until well browned, then turn and brown the other side 2-4 min.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Move patties to a baking tray dip side down and bake at 150 °C (130 °C fan) for 6-10 min until 71 °C in the centre; rest 5 min.

steps.title: Toast
steps.text: Heat the grill to high with a shelf 15 cm below, grill the 4 buns cut side up for about 1 min.

steps.title: Top
steps.text: Spread onion jam on the bun tops, cover with grated Gruyère and grill about 2 min until bubbling.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Place the patties in the buns with frisée leaves.

tips: Stir frequently during cooking to prevent burning and ensure even caramelisation.
The dip in the centre helps patties cook through evenly and stay juicy.
safety: Always check the centre reaches 71 °C with a thermometer inserted through the side.
storage: Cooked patties keep for 2 days refrigerated; the onion jam can be made up to 3 days ahead. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
